継.meaning: Grandma's will says only: 'Pull the <part>thread</part>.' You find it tied to a <part>pole</part> in her barn, give it a tug, and a trapdoor drops a mountain of <part>rice</part> on your head, plus her secret recipe book. It's all yours to <kanji>inherit</kanji>.
継.on: Recipe number one is her famous rice <sound>ca</sound>ke.
継.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' you sneeze in the rice dust, then take up the family cooking for <sound>goo</sound>d.

競.meaning: Twin boys argue over which one is the <part>big brother</part>. Each climbs onto a box to <part>stand</part> taller, then onto a ladder, then up onto the chimney. Mum sighs from the garden: they turn everything into a race. They always <kanji>compete</kanji>.
競.on: Up on the chimney the twins start a new contest: who can shout '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!' with the longest start. Mum hears the first part held across the whole garden.
競.kun: They even race to peel a <sound>ki</sound>wi and pull on a <sound>so</sound>ck.

浮.meaning: A <part>stork</part> forgets how to fly, so it lies on its back on the pond, wings out, and lets the <part>water drops</part> carry it along. Fish swim underneath, ducks climb aboard like it's a raft. It isn't swimming at all, just <kanji>floating</kanji>.
浮.on: It says the pond is as comfy as a rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton.
浮.kun: A frog rides on its tummy, slurping a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don.

村.meaning: A family of hedgehogs lives in one hollow <part>tree</part>. Every morning they tee off from the roots with a tiny <part>golf club</part>, and wherever the acorn lands, they build a new hut. After a year there are fifty huts: a whole <kanji>village</kanji>.
村.on: Their mayor wears a <sound>som</sound>brero made from one big leaf.
村.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se wanders in and asks for a hut too, and the hedgehogs cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

囲.meaning: A frog at the bottom of a <part>well</part> looks up and sees a <part>cage</part> being lowered over the top, then a ring of curious ducks around the cage, then a ring of goats around the ducks. Everyone wants a look. Rings and rings of them <kanji>surround</kanji> it.
囲.on: Down in the water, an <sound>ee</sound>l coils round the frog as well.
囲.kun: Then a <sound>ca</sound>rt full of <sound>koa</sound>las rolls up and joins the ring.

節.meaning: A wizard can grow <part>bamboo</part> in an <part>instant</part>: zap, a stalk shoots up. But it grows in jerks, stop, start, stop, and each stop leaves a hard little ring round the stem. Count the rings to know how many spells. Each ring is a <kanji>node</kanji>.
節.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter sniffs every ring and barks once at each.
節.kun: Then the wizard curls up on a <sound>fu</sound>ton stuffed with <sound>shee</sound>p's wool.

植.meaning: A robot gardener lowers a baby <part>tree</part> into a hole, then checks it with a laser ten times to be sure it stands perfectly <part>straight</part>. One wobble and it pulls it out and starts again. Six hours later the robot finally manages to <kanji>plant</kanji> it.
植.on: Then it waters the soil and gets an electric <sound>shock</sound>.
植.kun: To help the tree grow, it buries a warm bowl of <sound>u</sound>don by the roots.
